MEASURED 2026-08-26T15:32Z, and it completes today's 14:31Z finding from the opposite direction. That earlier run proved 1-minute bars are revised after they close (a -95.5% volume revision with a changed OHLC) and noted revisions 'ran both up and down' without having measured a large up-side case. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE NEW LESSON, AND IT IS A HOLE IN THE EXISTING FIX. The 'end the trailing baseline ~10 minutes back' rule protects the DENOMINATOR and nothing else. A provisional bar in the last minutes of the CANDIDATE window sits inside the numerator and outside a baseline that already ended ten minutes ago, so its revision is ONE-SIDED by construction. Measured exactly here: the revision moved the candidate 5-minute bar +28.6% (37,572 -> 48,331) while moving the baseline -0.11% (94,849 -> 94,749), lifting the confirmation reading from 39.7% to 51.0% of baseline. THE FIX, symmetric with the one already in the playbook: the final bar of a candidate window is the single bar most likely to be provisional AND the one whose revision cannot be offset. So either end the CANDIDATE window ~10 minutes back as well, or double-read its constituent minutes before letting it confirm. This run did the latter -- two fetches a minute apart, merged, disagreements resolved to the later read.

HONEST SCOPE, and it is what makes the audit credible: this changed NO decision today. The price clause failed outright, and 51% of baseline still fails the volume clause decisively. A filter's inputs can only be audited honestly on a day the correction does not flip the answer -- and the uncorrected 39.7% would have supported a stronger 'volume has collapsed' claim than the data actually carries, which is the small dishonesty this catch prevents.

volume_clause_denominator_collapse.title: A TRAILING-LOCAL VOLUME BASELINE INVERTS IN A DECAYING TAPE: THE CLAUSE GETS EASIER EXACTLY WHERE IT SHOULD GET HARDER. Measured 2026-08-26T15:52Z on the session's first clean bullish fire.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.measurement: QQQ 15:40-15:44Z candidate bucket = 98,957 shares (read B; read A 100,833, agreeing within 1.9%). Against the settled trailing-30-ending-10-back baseline of 66,144 it reads 149.6% and CONFIRMS. volume_clause_denominator_collapse.mechanism: The 2026-08-25 calibration rule correctly replaced a session-average denominator with a trailing-local one, because the opening hour's 254,448/bar made midday fires impossible. That fix is right and stays. What nobody checked is the other end: a trailing-local mean tracks a DECAYING tape downward, so as participation drains the bar to clear falls with it. In a pre-event vacuum the clause stops asking 'did participation arrive' and starts asking 'is this bar busier than the vacuum' -- which any drift back toward normal satisfies. The filter is self-fulfilling exactly when the tape is least informative.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.why_it_survived: Both denominator defects are invisible from outcomes and point in OPPOSITE directions, so neither is detectable by counting fires. A session-average baseline vetoes everything and looks like discipline; a collapsed local baseline confirms everything and looks like the filter finally working. The 15:30Z run predicted a clean fire would FAIL on volume and treated a volume-confirmed break as 'far more informative than usual' -- exactly backwards, and it was refuted fifteen minutes later. A run that inherits that framing reads a vacuum fire as high-conviction.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.detector: Report the candidate bar's volume in ABSOLUTE terms alongside the ratio, and test it against the session's OWN earlier baselines as well as the trailing-30 mean. Confirmation requires BOTH: at or above the trailing local mean AND not materially below the session's established bucket rate. A bar that clears the local baseline while sitting under the session's own typical bucket is baseline collapse, not participation -- decline it and say which of the two it was.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.honest_scope: This changed no decision on the day it was found: the fire was declined on five independent merits (magnitude 0.044%, a mid-range level, both MAs overhead and untouched, ex-gap IV/RV 1.1697, no catalyst), and the follow-through reverted to 103% of baseline with price flat, so the trade was bad on the tape as well as on the filter. That is the only condition under which a filter's inputs can be audited credibly -- the same standard the 2026-08-25 calibration finding set for itself.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.class: Same family as every denominator finding in CLAUDE.md: a constant or a window encoded an assumption about a moving thing, nothing errored, and the wrong behaviour was indistinguishable from the right one. Here the assumption was that a locally-calibrated baseline is always the conservative choice. It is not; it is conservative in a rising tape and permissive in a draining one.

But a 30-DTE board spanning an event blends event premium with ordinary positioning and dilutes the event across a much longer window, so its level is a poor proxy for what the market expects the event ITSELF to do. Measured on NVDA hours before its print: the 2026-08-28 210 straddle (the first expiry after the event) priced an implied move of +/-5.806% (12.20 on 210.135 spot) versus +/-5.975% from the prior session's settled closes (12.73 on 213.05) -- CONTRACTING -- while the 30-DTE board rose 0.4108 -> 0.4144 and every run that day called it 'event premium peaking into the print'. DETECTOR, and it is two quotes: for any name with a known event inside the hold window, quote the ATM straddle on the FIRST expiry after the event and divide by spot; compare it to the SAME straddle's prior-session close. Rising = the event is being bid; flat or falling = expectations have stopped expanding regardless of what the 30-DTE row says. THE SHAPE, which is this file's most-repeated defect arriving through a new door: a correct measurement of the wrong board was allowed to answer a question it was never measuring, and nothing errored -- the conclusion was even right. Same family as the IV-sweep spread that became a liquidity verdict (2026-08-24) and the ATM quote that became an affordability verdict (2026-08-17). HONEST SCOPE: this changed no decision -- NVDA CORE is barred on the print, the exit engine and an n=12-record ex-gap ratio regardless -- which is the only condition under which auditing your own inputs is credible.

Today's fire passed every filter the 2026-08-25/26 calibration work built (structural level not a desk-drawn box, completed close, held on following bars, volume clearing both the trailing-local and the session-rate denominators, index tape agreeing, chain 5x inside the liquidity gate, right delta, inside the size band) and was still not worth taking, because +20% required a 2.16-point SPY move against a 2.28-point session range with 3.1 hours left, and the best structural level on the chart paid only +18.5%. THE TEST, one line of arithmetic off the live greeks: solve the underlying move implied by the track's MINIMUM profit target, then compare it to (a) the session's realised range and (b) the distance to the next genuine structural level. If the minimum target needs more than roughly the session's whole range, or if reaching the best nearby level still misses the minimum target, DECLINE -- the level is too shallow to trade regardless of how cleanly it confirmed. This is the TACTICAL analogue of the CORE breakeven-scrutiny rule ('if the leg pays roughly nothing at the price where the thesis says to bank profit, skip it'), and the two should be read as one principle: a vehicle that is cheap, liquid and correctly triggered still supplies no edge if the payoff at the thesis target is not there. _DURABLE_FINDINGS_2026-08-26.equity_mechanical_exit_is_a_TAKE_PROFIT_: PROMOTE TO CLAUDE.md BEFORE DELETING THIS SESSION KEY. The v8 prompt's equity clause reads 'a target hit or RSI2>=70 swing bounce on a ledger position = bank it autonomously', and read literally that fires on ANY position whose RSI2 crosses 70 -- winners and losers alike. On the very first run holding the authority (2026-08-26T18:15Z) it fired on PNC at RSI2 78.5 while the position sat 0.34% UNDERWATER, i.e. the literal reading would have realized a loss on a technical bounce. That is not what the trigger is. HARD RULE 5 defines it as a TAKE-PROFIT ('Take-profit fires on a target hit or an RSI2>=70 swing bounce'), states that 'a winner can then only ever be sold for a locked-in gain', and routes underwater names to THESIS management with no price stop at all. report.py already encodes the distinction in its own label -- 'EXIT-INTO-STRENGTH (underwater -- optional)' with 'policy default is hold-on-thesis' -- so the ledger, the playbook and the report all agree and only the prompt's compressed wording is ambiguous. RULE FOR THE RELAY: the autonomous equity mechanical exit is a PROFIT-BANKING authority. Gate it on price > entry. An RSI2>=70 print on an underwater position is an OPTIONAL exit-into-strength and therefore requires the same discretionary judgment as any other loss-taking -- which under HARD RULE 5 means a HARD RULE 7 thesis break, not a technical trigger. THE TRANSFERABLE SHAPE, and it is this file's most-repeated one: a newly-granted authority arrives with wording compressed for brevity, and the first run to hold it is the run most likely to read the compression literally. When a new prompt's one-line summary of a rule is broader than the rule it summarizes, the RULE governs -- and the governance clause says so explicitly ('where either is stricter, the stricter rule applies'). Check the summarized rule before exercising a power for the first time.

durable_findings.neighbour_ratio_is_a_DENOMINATOR_FREE_pr:
This file has spent three sessions arguing about the volume DENOMINATOR: the session-average baseline was too strict (inflated by the opening hour, 2026-08-25T16:05Z); the trailing-local baseline inverts in a decaying tape (2026-08-26T15:52Z); anomaly-exclusion biases in the same false-positive direction (2026-08-27T14:25Z). All three are disputes about what to divide BY. The 14:27Z break needed no denominator at all: 2,698 against immediate neighbours of 28,980 and 24,243 fails on inspection against ANY baseline anyone in that argument could have constructed.
THE PREFILTER, and it costs nothing because the bars are already in hand: before computing any trailing mean, compare the candidate breakout bar to the two bars immediately either side of it. If it is below roughly half of BOTH neighbours, decline on that alone and skip the baseline computation entirely -- no choice of denominator can rescue it, so no choice of denominator needs defending. Compute the trailing mean only for bars that clear this, i.e. only where the calibration question is actually load-bearing.
WHY THIS IS WORTH MORE THAN ANOTHER CALIBRATION FIX: every prior fix made the filter more correct and left it equally arguable, and each corrected filter then failed on a better setup. A test that is invariant to the disputed parameter cannot be argued with. SCOPE, stated honestly: this prefilter only ever REJECTS. It says nothing about a bar that clears its neighbours -- that case still needs the full dual test and the settled-baseline discipline, unchanged.

The 2026-08-26T17:19Z capstone concluded: 'do not open TACTICAL breakout scalps into an unresolved scheduled catalyst', on the mechanism that 'pre-event positioning flow is not directional' -- participation arrives at a level to de-risk, then stops, because nobody expresses a view before the number. Breaks are still failing -- the ninth attempt fired and reversed inside three minutes today, on the same signature. A pre-event vacuum cannot explain a post-event failure.
PROPOSED REPLACEMENT MECHANISM: BREADTH. QQQ is +0.956% and roughly 87% of that is two names (NVDA ~0.70pp, MSFT ~0.14pp). An index that is 87% a single-stock proxy has no broad participation to carry a level break, because the other ninety-odd constituents are not going anywhere -- which is exactly what the volume signature keeps saying, in a form the desk kept reading as a measurement problem rather than as the finding itself. The thin-volume breaks and the narrow leadership are ONE fact seen twice, not two facts.
DETECTOR, testable and cheap: before taking any index breakout, compute the share of the index's move attributable to its top one or two contributors. Above roughly 70%, treat the index's own levels as carrying no information -- trade the LEADER on its own levels, or do not trade. This also explains cleanly why the arc's failures cluster on QQQ rather than SPY: QQQ's concentration is far higher, so its levels degrade first.
EPISTEMIC STATUS, stated plainly so the next instance does not inherit this as settled: ONE observation, and the contribution arithmetic rests on ~9% / ~8% index weights that are carried-forward approximations rather than measured. This is a HYPOTHESIS THAT OUTPERFORMS THE INCUMBENT ONE, not an established fact. It is falsifiable and should be tested: if an index break fires cleanly on a genuinely broad day (top-2 contribution under ~40%) and holds, that supports it; if breaks keep failing on a broad day, breadth is not the mechanism either and the desk should stop theorising and simply stop trading index breakouts in this regime.

byte_identity_is_NOT_a_reliable_detector.the_rule: Keep the identity test as a fast POSITIVE indicator -- when it fires the bar is defective, full stop. Never use it as the screen.
